sample_unit: recommendation-level evaluations by neurosurgeons (59 cases, 22 raters)

links.outcome: Appropriateness-based acceptability of LLM neurosurgical approach suggestions on expert-curated vignettes
links.effect: Acceptability 76.7% for text (95% CI 68.5-84.1) and 72.4% for MRI-augmented prompts (95% CI 64.2-80.2); acceptability above 70% not established; intra-axial superficial lowest at 56.5%.
links.quote: Appropriateness-based acceptability was 76.7% for text (95% CI 68.5-84.1) and 72.4% for MRI-augmented prompts (95% CI 64.2-80.2); although both point estimates exceeded the exploratory 70% benchmark, the confidence intervals extended below it, so acceptability above 70% at the population level was not established.

links.outcome: Clinically important errors in lowest-rated LLM suggestions requiring verification
links.effect: Error analysis of lowest-rated cases revealed clinically important failures including incorrect laterality, so outputs require expert oversight.
links.quote: Critically, error analysis of the lowest-rated cases revealed clinically important failures including incorrect laterality, underscoring that these outputs require expert oversight.

links.outcome: LLM suggestion ratings varied across tumor categories
links.effect: Pituitary highest (87.4%) and intra-axial superficial lowest (56.5%; p=0.019).
links.quote: Ratings varied markedly by tumor category: pituitary highest (87.4%) and intra-axial superficial lowest (56.5%; p=0.019).

links.outcome: Performance change when MRI was appended to text prompt
links.effect: Text prompts rated higher than MRI-augmented prompts, persisting under clustering (p=0.020), driven mainly by LLM-3.
links.quote: Text prompts were rated higher than MRI-augmented prompts, persisting under clustering (p=0.020) and driven mainly by LLM-3.

links.outcome: Inter-rater reliability of neurosurgeon ratings (Krippendorff's alpha)
links.effect: Agreement low overall (α=0.270), higher among specialists (α=0.439) than trainees (α=0.173).
links.quote: Inter-rater agreement was low overall (α=0.270), higher among specialists (α=0.439) than trainees (α=0.173).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates multimodal LLM performance on neurosurgical approach planning using clinical vignettes with clinician (neurosurgeon) evaluation, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
